description: Commit-replay edit tasks on spring-framework (issue #183). Hand-written part: which commits, the change description the agent gets (drafted by an agent from the commit message and linked issue, reviewed by a second agent for leakage and solvability), the primary files and, where the default does not fit, the test command. Everything else is derived from the commit by commit_replay.py build.

tasks.question: SimpleEvaluationContext deliberately restricts SpEL to a subset of its features, but by default it converts values with the framework's shared default conversion service, which can convert a value by reflectively invoking constructors and methods of the target type (a single-argument constructor, static valueOf/of/from, find<Entity>, or to<TargetType>() on the source). By default, SimpleEvaluationContext should instead use a restricted conversion service: one with the same converters as the default except its Object-to-Object converters (ObjectToObjectConverter and IdToEntityConverter). Common conversions such as numbers, booleans, enums, UUID, collections and arrays must keep working, and an index, map key or property value conversion that is no longer supported should fail with a ConverterNotFoundException as root cause; a method whose arguments can no longer be converted is simply not found, as for any other inconvertible argument. A TypeConverter or ConversionService registered via withTypeConverter(...) or withConversionService(...) on the builder is still used as-is. Add `public <S, T> Builder withConverter(Class<S> sourceType, Class<T> targetType, Converter<? super S, ? extends T> converter)` to SimpleEvaluationContext.Builder: it may be called several times and adds converters on top of the default (restricted) conversion service, and build() throws an IllegalStateException if withConverter() was combined with withConversionService() or withTypeConverter(), in either order. Also add `public static final String REFLECTIVE_CONVERSION_PROPERTY_NAME = "spring.expression.reflectiveConversion"` to SimpleEvaluationContext: when this flag is set (JVM system property or SpringProperties), the default is the standard, unrestricted conversion service again, and withConverter() then adds to an unrestricted one. The flag is not cached: it is consulted each time a default conversion service is needed for a new context, so it can be toggled at runtime.
tasks.rationale: The commit gives SimpleEvaluationContext a restricted default ConversionService (DefaultConversionService minus Object->Object converters), adds Builder.withConverter() and a SpringProperties flag that restores the old behaviour. SimpleEvaluationContext is the primary file. Dependents: a maintenance comment in DefaultConversionService (spring-core) next to the reflective converters, the SpEL reference docs (evaluation.adoc security section and type conversion note) and the Spring properties table in appendix.adoc.
tasks.notes: No linked issue. Tests check SpelMessage codes (TYPE_CONVERSION_ERROR, EXCEPTION_DURING_PROPERTY_WRITE, METHOD_NOT_FOUND) and a ConverterNotFoundException root cause, which follow naturally from removing the converters. reflectiveConversionProperty toggles a SpringProperties flag at runtime, so an implementation that caches the flag statically fails; the description says so. The only spring-core change is a comment, so the dependent check for it scores comment-only edits.

review.comment: All test-needed API is stated: Builder.withConverter(Class<S>,Class<T>,Converter<? super S,? extends T>), REFLECTIVE_CONVERSION_PROPERTY_NAME='spring.expression.reflectiveConversion', IllegalStateException on combination in either order, ConverterNotFoundException root cause, flag read at build time (test toggles SpringProperties). Naming ObjectToObjectConverter/IdToEntityConverter and 'DefaultConversionService without its Object-to-Object converters' nearly gives away the solution (removeConvertible(Object,Object)) and points at DefaultConversionService, which is a gold dependent (maintenance comment only). The commit message says the same, so it is acceptable issue wording; mild over-specification. Dependents (DefaultConversionService comment, evaluation.adoc, appendix.adoc) are not mentioned.

after_pr_review.comment: All wrong facts are minor and none blocks solving. Reworded sentence is fine: 'same converters as the default except its Object-to-Object converters' is exact (ObjectToObjectConverter and IdToEntityConverter are the only Object->Object converters at the parent; FallbackObjectToStringConverter is Object->String and stays, which 'text = builder' needs). DefaultConversionService is not named; the two converter names lead to it by one grep, but the change there is comment only. withConverter signature equals ConverterRegistry.addConverter; removeConvertible, SpringProperties.setFlag/getFlag exist at the parent. Dependents that can be scored are only the two adoc pages and the test: weak as a dependents task.
not_enforced: spring-core/.../DefaultConversionService.java (comment only; cannot be enforced). There are no other gold code dependents: editing SimpleEvaluationContext alone passes.

tasks.question: HTTP client observations use the request method name as the value of the low-cardinality "method" key, falling back to "none" only when no request could be created. With RestTemplate and RestClient, the default observation convention reports any method name as-is, so a non-standard method such as HttpMethod.valueOf("CUSTOM") becomes its own tag value, which can blow up metric cardinality. The default server request observation conventions already guard against arbitrary method names. Apply the same guard to the framework's HTTP client observations: report the method name only when it is one of the standard HttpMethod values, and "none" otherwise.
tasks.rationale: The commit makes the default client observation conventions emit method=none for non-standard HTTP methods. The primary file is the spring-web convention used by RestTemplate/RestClient. The dependent is the same-named WebClient convention in spring-webflux (org.springframework.web.reactive.function.client), plus a one-line clarification in observability.adoc.
tasks.notes: Scope: the description says 'HTTP client observations' and gives the class name, which exists in both spring-web and spring-webflux (different packages); the commit message names RestTemplate, RestClient and WebClient. The webflux test fails unless the agent also finds the WebClient convention, which is the dependent this task checks. No linked issue.

review.comment: Solvable: the tests only assert method=none for HttpMethod.valueOf("CUSTOM") on both client conventions, and no new public names are needed. 'HTTP client observations' plus 'default client request observation convention' is fine scope wording; the same-named WebFlux convention is left for the agent to find. The primary file (spring-web convention) is correct. The test_command covers both overlay classes. The only problem is the documentation sentence.

second.comment: Tests need no new API: MockClientHttpRequest(HttpMethod, String, Object...), ClientRequest.create(HttpMethod, URI), both test createContext helpers, and KeyValue "method"/"none" exist at the parent or are stated. 'HTTP client observations' is an allowed scope phrase and is enough to derive the reactive counterpart. Gold non-test files: both conventions plus observability.adoc (the parent adoc row says only 'if the request could not be created').

tasks.question: Code that handles an exception can record it on the server request observation by calling setError on the ServerRequestObservationContext, for example via ServerHttpObservationFilter.findObservationContext(request) or ServerRequestObservationContext.findCurrent(attributes). That error reaches the metrics, but Observation.error(Throwable) is never called, so ObservationHandlers such as the tracing handler are not notified and the server span is not marked as failed. Code outside the filter cannot call Observation.error reliably itself. Add `public static void recordHandledException(HttpServletRequest request, Throwable error)` to ServerHttpObservationFilter and `public static void recordHandledException(Map<String, Object> attributes, Throwable error)` to ServerRequestObservationContext (for the reactive exchange attributes). The recorded exception must be reported once via Observation.error when the exchange completes, before the observation is stopped, also when the request completes asynchronously. Both methods are no-ops when there is no observation for the request or exchange; in that case they must not add any request attribute or map entry. Spring MVC's and WebFlux's own exception handling, which currently records server errors (5xx) on the observation context, should use the new methods.
tasks.rationale: The commit adds recordHandledException to the Servlet observation filter and to the reactive observation context; the filter (and, through an existing exchange attribute, HttpWebHandlerAdapter) reports the exception via Observation.error when the exchange completes. Primary files are the two spring-web types the tests call. Dependents: the Spring MVC call sites (ResponseStatusExceptionResolver, ExceptionHandlerExceptionResolver, ResponseEntityExceptionHandler, DefaultHandlerExceptionResolver), the WebFlux ResponseEntityExceptionHandler, the two framework-docs UserController snippets and observability.adoc.
tasks.notes: spring-webmvc tests left out: they need a build change from the commit (testImplementation io.micrometer:micrometer-observation-test in spring-webmvc.gradle) that a description cannot fairly ask for, and they rely on the new ObservedExchange test helper, which is not a test class. They also pass on the parent, because the resolvers already call context.setError and the helper reads context.getError(). The webflux ResponseEntityExceptionHandlerTests probably pass on the parent too and are kept only as a regression guard. Scope stated as 'Spring MVC's and WebFlux's own exception handling'; no classes named.

review.comment: Both static signatures, the no-op rule with no attribute or entry added (asserted by both 'without observation' tests), reporting via Observation.error before stop, and async completion are all stated. The reactive side can reuse the parent's HttpWebHandlerAdapter handling of the 'ExceptionHandlingWebHandler.handledException' attribute (the agent can find this) or change the adapter, so either way works. test_command leaves out the spring-webmvc overlay tests (ObservedExchange etc.). That is correct: they need the build-file change that adds micrometer-observation-test to spring-webmvc.gradle, which no description can fairly ask for. As a result the MVC dependents (resolvers, ResponseEntityExceptionHandler) are scored only through file comparison, not by tests. The webflux ResponseEntityExceptionHandlerTests may already pass at the parent, because context.setError satisfies hasError. The spring-web tests fail at the parent (the method is missing). Not over-specified.

tasks.weak_test: A passing solution may skip all MVC and WebFlux call sites (webmvc tests are not run; the WebFlux test asserts only the context error). Even the core requirement is unchecked: recordHandledException implemented as context.setError(error) passes every listed test, because hasError and the 'exception' key value come from the context and no handler's onError / Observation.error call is asserted. Not enforced: UserController.java, UserController.java, ResponseEntityExceptionHandler.java, ResponseStatusExceptionResolver.java, ExceptionHandlerExceptionResolver.java, ResponseEntityExceptionHandler.java, DefaultHandlerExceptionResolver.java.

tasks.question: SpelParserConfiguration.DEFAULT_MAX_EXPRESSION_NESTING_DEPTH (currently 1000) is meant to make the SpEL parser throw a descriptive SpelParseException before a deeply nested expression exhausts the call stack. Before the parser has been JIT-compiled, though, a thread with the common 1 MB or 2 MB stack throws a StackOverflowError after roughly 450 to 950 levels of nesting, before the limit is reached. Real-world SpEL expressions rarely nest more than a few levels deep. Lower the default maximum nesting depth to 200, so that an expression nested exactly to the default depth parses successfully on a thread with a 1 MB stack, and one level more fails with the usual nesting-depth SpelParseException. Applications that need more can still configure a higher limit via SpelParserConfiguration.builder().maximumNestingDepth(...).
tasks.rationale: The commit lowers DEFAULT_MAX_EXPRESSION_NESTING_DEPTH from 1000 to 200 and documents why. SpelParserConfiguration holds the constant. The only dependent is the SpEL reference doc (evaluation.adoc), which states the old default of 1,000.
tasks.notes: The task is small: a constant change plus a docs dependent. The new test runs the parser on a thread with a 1 MB stack, so whether it fails on the parent depends on the JVM and JIT state; at depth 1000 it should overflow reliably. The test asserts the existing message 'SpEL expression nesting depth exceeds the threshold of N'.

review.comment: Faithful to the issue; DEFAULT_MAX_EXPRESSION_NESTING_DEPTH and builder().maximumNestingDepth(...) exist at the parent; the new value 200 is stated. Trivial one-constant change; the only dependent is evaluation.adoc ('cannot exceed 1,000 by default'), which is not mentioned.

tasks.question: When a controller or @ExceptionHandler method returns a ProblemDetail, either directly as the response body or as the body of a ResponseEntity/HttpEntity, the framework sets its instance property to the current request path if the application has not set it. For example, Spring MVC's RequestResponseBodyMethodProcessor does this. RFC 9457 defines instance as a URI reference that identifies the specific occurrence of the problem, not the request URL, so this default is wrong and not useful to clients. The framework should no longer populate instance itself: it stays null unless the application sets it, and a value set by the application is still rendered as-is.
tasks.rationale: The commit removes the code that defaults ProblemDetail.instance to the request path. The description points at RequestResponseBodyMethodProcessor (Spring MVC, @ResponseBody case). Dependents: HttpEntityMethodProcessor (MVC, ResponseEntity case), WebFlux ResponseBodyResultHandler and ResponseEntityResultHandler, and the RFC 9457 sections in both the MVC and WebFlux reference docs (ann-rest-exceptions.adoc).
tasks.notes: Scope is not stated: the issue was filed against Spring MVC, and WebFlux has to be found by the agent (four webflux test classes check it). Tests assert exact JSON/XML bodies without 'instance'. Integration tests (RequestMappingExceptionHandlingIntegrationTests, ResourceHttpRequestHandlerIntegrationTests) start servers and are somewhat slower.

review.comment: Clean. It names only the primary RequestResponseBodyMethodProcessor, plus the generic phrase 'the framework'. The phrase 'directly as the response body or as the body of a ResponseEntity/HttpEntity' is behavioural scope as a user would put it; it hints at the HttpEntity path but names no class. WebFlux handlers and both adoc pages are left for the agent to find. The tests only drop instance expectations or assert null; no new API. Primary file is correct. The test_command covers all 7 overlay classes. ResourceHttpRequestHandlerIntegrationTests and RequestMappingExceptionHandlingIntegrationTests are integration tests, but they are deterministic.

tasks.question: AbstractNestablePropertyAccessor resolves a nested property path such as "a.b.c.d" recursively, one level per path segment, with no limit on the depth. A long enough path, for example against a self-referential type, exhausts the stack with a StackOverflowError that gives no useful diagnostics. Constructor binding via DataBinder.construct() has the same problem, since it builds nested constructor arguments recursively through a nested path, including elements of indexed and mapped parameters. Add a maximum nesting depth: `int DEFAULT_MAX_NESTED_PATH_DEPTH = 100` plus `void setMaxNestedPathDepth(int)` and `int getMaxNestedPathDepth()` on ConfigurablePropertyAccessor, and `setMaxNestedPathDepth(int)`/`getMaxNestedPathDepth()` on DataBinder, which applies the limit to the property accessor it uses (bean property or direct field access) and to constructor binding. The nesting depth is the number of intermediate properties traversed ("address.country.name" has depth 2); a path at exactly the limit is allowed, a deeper one throws an InvalidPropertyException whose message ends with "Nesting depth of property path exceeds the maximum of <limit>". The limit applies whether or not autoGrowNestedPaths is enabled. A value of 0 disables nested paths but still allows simple, indexed and mapped access. Negative values are rejected with an IllegalArgumentException with the message "'maxNestedPathDepth' must not be negative". Like setAutoGrowCollectionLimit, DataBinder.setMaxNestedPathDepth must throw an IllegalStateException containing "DataBinder is already initialized - call setMaxNestedPathDepth before other configuration methods" once the binding result has been initialized. Resolution of a nested path must keep recursing through the protected getPropertyAccessorForPropertyPath(String) method, so that subclass overrides are still invoked at every level.
tasks.rationale: The commit tracks nesting depth per nested property accessor and in DataBinder's recursive constructor binding, and throws InvalidPropertyException past a configurable limit (default 100). Primary files are the three types the description names (the accessor where the recursion lives, the interface with the new API, DataBinder). Dependents: AbstractPropertyAccessor (holds and validates the setting), BeanPropertyBindingResult and DirectFieldBindingResult (new constructor argument passed through to their accessors; the direct field access test needs it), and the data-binding reference doc (data-binding.adoc).
tasks.notes: AbstractPropertyAccessorTests is abstract: its new @Nested MaxNestedPathDepthTests run through the concrete subclasses BeanWrapperTests and DirectFieldAccessorTests, so the command runs those two instead of the abstract class. Tests assert exact messages (ending/containing). The test for the getPropertyAccessorForPropertyPath override passes on the parent; it is a regression guard, hence the last sentence of the description. The stack-overflow tests use paths 100,000 segments deep.

review.comment: Every new name the tests use is stated: DEFAULT_MAX_NESTED_PATH_DEPTH=100, set/getMaxNestedPathDepth on ConfigurablePropertyAccessor (tests call them on AbstractPropertyAccessor; adding them there is a dependent) and on DataBinder, the message suffix, the negative-value IAE message, and the DataBinder 'already initialized' ISE text. The depth semantics (limit inclusive, 0 still allows simple/indexed/mapped access) are also stated. The last sentence (keep recursing through the protected getPropertyAccessorForPropertyPath) borders on over-specification. It is justified: BeanWrapperTests counts 3 invocations of an override, and a depth-threading private recursion would fail that test. The parent already recurses this way, so the sentence only forbids a regression. The test_command adds DirectFieldAccessorTests, which is not in the overlay; that is correct because it inherits from the changed abstract AbstractPropertyAccessorTests. The deep-path tests (100_000 segments) are deterministic once the depth check runs before the recursion.

tasks.untested: In DataBinder only nested record arguments are tested for constructor binding; a passing solution may omit the limit for indexed and mapped parameters (createList/createMap/createArray/createIndexedValue), which the question explicitly requires. DataBinder's own rejection of negative values is not tested either.

tasks.question: SpelParserConfiguration has accumulated many overloaded constructors, ending in an 8-parameter one (compilerMode, compilerClassLoader, autoGrowNullReferences, autoGrowCollections, maximumAutoGrowSize, maximumExpressionLength, maximumOperations, maximumBigPowerBits). Call sites are unlabeled lists of booleans and ints, and overriding one setting means repeating every other default. Introduce a fluent builder like the one on SimpleEvaluationContext: `SpelParserConfiguration.builder()` returns a public static nested `SpelParserConfiguration.Builder` with `compilerMode(SpelCompilerMode)`, `compilerClassLoader(@Nullable ClassLoader)`, no-arg opt-ins `autoGrowNullReferences()` and `autoGrowCollections()`, `maximumAutoGrowSize(int)`, `maximumExpressionLength(int)`, `maximumOperations(int)`, `maximumBigPowerBits(int)` and `build()`. Each setter validates its argument as soon as it is called and throws an IllegalArgumentException for a null compiler mode, a negative maximumAutoGrowSize, or a maximumExpressionLength, maximumOperations or maximumBigPowerBits that is not positive. Also add `SpelParserConfiguration.withDefaults()` as shorthand for `builder().build()`. The builder's defaults match the no-arg constructor, including the SpringProperties-driven defaults for compiler mode, maximum operations and maximum big-power bits; the one exception is maximumAutoGrowSize, which defaults to 256 (like DataBinder's default auto-grow collection limit) instead of Integer.MAX_VALUE. The framework itself should create its configurations through the new API instead of the constructors. The existing constructors stay unchanged (in particular they still accept a negative maximumAutoGrowSize) and are not deprecated.
tasks.rationale: The commit adds SpelParserConfiguration.builder()/Builder/withDefaults() and moves internal call sites to it. SpelParserConfiguration is the primary file. Dependents are the internal call sites switched to the builder: SpelExpressionParser's no-arg constructor, ExpressionState's convenience constructors, and StandardBeanExpressionResolver in spring-context. These switches don't change behaviour and no test checks them. The SpEL reference docs (evaluation.adoc) are also a dependent.
tasks.notes: On the 7.0.x line: the parent has no maximumNestingDepth, so the linked issue's mention of a 9-parameter constructor does not apply and the description says 8 parameters. Most changed test classes only switch from constructors to the builder, so they just need the API to compile. SpelParserConfigurationTests also checks that the canonical constructor still accepts a negative maximumAutoGrowSize, so the agent must not add validation there; 'constructors stay unchanged' covers this. Dependent call sites are refactorings that no test checks.

review.comment: All new names are stated (builder(), Builder, 8 setters, build(), withDefaults(), default 256). Fix only the validation timing (see missing_for_tests) and drop 'build() should delegate to the existing canonical constructor' (implementation detail that invites the wrong validation placement). The legacy-constructor test canonicalConstructorDoesNotRejectNegativeMaximumAutoGrowSize requires the constructor to stay lenient; 'constructors stay unchanged' covers it, made explicit in the rewrite. Dependents (SpelExpressionParser, ExpressionState, StandardBeanExpressionResolver switched to the builder; evaluation.adoc) are behaviour-neutral refactors, so expect low dependent recall regardless of description quality.
review.applied: question replaced by the reviewer's rewrite

second.comment: Reason for fix: the question never asks to move any usage to the new API, but the non-test, non-doc dependents (StandardBeanExpressionResolver, ExpressionState, SpelExpressionParser) are only call-site migrations. At the parent these are the only main-code constructor usages outside the class itself. A correct, complete answer to the current text changes only SpelParserConfiguration and passes all tests, so dependent recall would measure guessing. One scope sentence fixes this without naming a file. Solvability: every name and signature in the test diff is stated (builder(), withDefaults(), nested Builder, all eight setters including the no-arg ones and @Nullable class loader, build(), IllegalArgumentException cases at setter time, default 256); no messages asserted. LegacyConstructorTests and EvaluationTests (maxOperations SpringProperty read per instance) pass with parent constructors and a builder matching them. Facts verified: 8 constructors, the 8-arg parameter order, no negative maximumAutoGrowSize check, DataBinder.DEFAULT_AUTO_GROW_COLLECTION_LIMIT = 256, SimpleEvaluationContext has a nested public static final Builder. SimpleEvaluationContext and DataBinder are not gold files, so naming them is no leak.

tasks.question: A SpEL power operation on a BigDecimal or BigInteger base (for example `#bd ^ 1000000`) can be extremely expensive in time and memory, and nothing limits it. Add a configurable limit on the estimated result size of such power operations. The estimate in bits is the bit length of the base multiplied by the exponent, where the bit length is BigInteger.bitLength() for a BigInteger and the bit length of unscaledValue() for a BigDecimal. A result exactly at the limit is allowed. If the estimate exceeds the limit, throw a SpelEvaluationException at the position of the power operator with the new message code `SpelMessage.MAX_BIG_POWER_RESULT_EXCEEDED`, whose inserts are, in order, the base bit length, the exponent and the configured maximum. In SpelParserConfiguration, add `DEFAULT_MAX_BIG_POWER_BITS = 1_000_000`, a new canonical constructor `SpelParserConfiguration(SpelCompilerMode, ClassLoader, boolean, boolean, int, int, int, int maximumBigPowerBits)` that rejects non-positive values, and `getMaximumBigPowerBits()`. The default can also be set globally via a JVM system property or Spring property named `spring.expression.maxBigPowerBits`, exposed as the constant `SPRING_EXPRESSION_MAX_BIG_POWER_BITS_PROPERTY_NAME`. Integer.MAX_VALUE removes the limit.
tasks.rationale: The commit limits BigDecimal/BigInteger power results in SpEL via a new SpelParserConfiguration setting (default 1,000,000 bits, overridable through SpringProperties) and a new SpelMessage. Primary files are the configuration class and SpelMessage, both named. Dependents: OperatorPower (the AST node that must do the check), the @see list in SpringProperties (spring-core), the parser-configuration section of evaluation.adoc and the Spring properties table in appendix.adoc.
tasks.notes: The commit message has a typo 'Closes ch-37034', read here as gh-37034. AbstractExpressionTests (an abstract test-support class that gains an evaluateAndCheckError overload) is left out of the test command; it is copied with the test files. Tests check the message code and its inserts (position 4, base bit length, exponent, max), not the message text. The BigDecimal bit-length detail (unscaledValue) is stated because the inserts assert 5 for BigDecimal 2.0.

review.comment: The tests need: the 8-arg constructor (positional), the SpelMessage.MAX_BIG_POWER_RESULT_EXCEEDED code, the insert order (base bit length, exponent, max) as ints, the error position at the operator (4 for '#bd ^ 4'), the inclusive limit, and the bit-length definition via unscaledValue() for BigDecimal (2.0 gives 5 bits). All are stated. The estimate formula looks like an implementation detail, but the boundary tests (15<=16, 20>16, 16==16) need it. The message text and number 1086 are not asserted, so omitting them is fine. The tests themselves add an evaluateAndCheckError overload, which comes in with the overlay.

tasks.question: FormHttpMessageConverter only reads and writes URL-encoded forms as a MultiValueMap, so a plain Map<String, String> (for example one created with Map.of(...)) cannot be used as a form body. FormHttpMessageConverter should support any Map for reading and writing application/x-www-form-urlencoded content. To allow this, the converter is declared as a SmartHttpMessageConverter<Object> instead of being typed to MultiValueMap<String, String>: read(...) returns Object, and write(...) accepts an Object that must be a Map. When the target type is not a MultiValueMap, reading returns a single-value Map that keeps only the first value for each key. canRead and canWrite accept Map, MultiValueMap and their implementations, with or without generics. Both methods only match a media type that one of the supported media types includes, so canWrite no longer accepts a wildcard such as */*. Writing a plain Map serializes each entry as name=value in the map's iteration order.
tasks.rationale: The commit widens FormHttpMessageConverter from MultiValueMap<String,String> to Object so Map payloads can be read and written, and makes canWrite use includes() like canRead. The primary file is the converter. Dependents are the call sites that now need a cast on read(...): FormContentFilter (spring-web), ContentRequestMatchers and AbstractMockHttpServletRequestBuilder (spring-test), plus the message-converters AsciiDoc page.
tasks.notes: The generic type change is stated because the test calls write(HashMap, MediaType, HttpOutputMessage), which only compiles with SmartHttpMessageConverter<Object>. The canWrite(*/*) == false change is stated because the test asserts it. writeFormFromMap asserts HashMap iteration order ("name+2=value+2&name+1=value+1"), which is deterministic for these keys. The spring-test call sites fail to compile without casts; the spring-web test run alone does not catch that, but a full build does.

review.comment: The type change to SmartHttpMessageConverter<Object> (read returns Object, write takes Object) is needed: the test calls write(HashMap) and casts read results. It also explains the casts needed in spring-test/FormContentFilter, but it names no dependents. Also stated: canRead/canWrite for Map, MultiValueMap and their subtypes with or without generics; includes() matching, so */* is rejected; a single-value Map for non-MultiValueMap targets; serialization in iteration order (writeFormFromMap relies on the deterministic HashMap order 'name+2=...&name+1=...', which is not flaky). One minor gap: cannotReadToMapsWhenMediaTypeMissing expects canRead(type, null) == false. This follows from 'only match a media type that one of the supported media types includes', because includes(null) is false, and the parent already behaves this way, so it is acceptable.

tasks.question: Spring's web frameworks use application/x-ndjson for streaming newline-delimited JSON, but application/jsonl (JSON Lines) is gaining popularity and may supersede it. Add JSON Lines as a well-known media type on MediaType, with the constants APPLICATION_JSONL and APPLICATION_JSONL_VALUE ("application/jsonl"). It must be supported everywhere application/x-ndjson is supported today. The JSON codecs list it among their default supported MIME types, directly after application/x-ndjson, and treat it as a streaming media type. Spring MVC streams a reactive multi-value return value as newline-delimited JSON with the content type application/jsonl when the client accepts application/jsonl, just as it does for application/x-ndjson.
tasks.rationale: The commit adds MediaType.APPLICATION_JSONL(_VALUE) and registers it next to NDJSON in every JSON codec (Jackson 3 and 2, Gson, Kotlin serialization, Protobuf JSON) and in Spring MVC's ReactiveTypeHandler. MediaType is the primary file. Dependents are the codec classes in spring-web, ReactiveTypeHandler and spring-mvc.xsd in spring-webmvc, and three AsciiDoc pages.
tasks.notes: Scope is stated ("everywhere application/x-ndjson is supported", Spring MVC streaming) without naming classes. The position after x-ndjson is stated because HttpMessageWriterViewTests uses containsExactly on the supported media types. The tests span two modules: spring-webflux (HttpMessageWriterViewTests) and spring-webmvc (ReactiveTypeHandlerTests).

review.comment: MediaType.APPLICATION_JSONL / APPLICATION_JSONL_VALUE stated; ordering 'directly after application/x-ndjson' is stated (HttpMessageWriterViewTests uses containsExactly). MVC content-type behaviour stated (ReactiveTypeHandlerTests). Not mentioned: spring-mvc.xsd, three adoc pages, the individual codecs - good for the dependent metric.

tasks.weak_test: A passing solution needs only MediaType, the default MIME types of JacksonJsonEncoder and ReactiveTypeHandler. All other codecs (Gson, Jackson 2, Jackson decoder, Kotlin, Protobuf) may be skipped, and 'treat it as a streaming media type' is not checked for any codec, including JacksonJsonEncoder. Not enforced: GsonEncoder.java, Jackson2CodecSupport.java, Jackson2JsonEncoder.java, JacksonJsonDecoder.java, KotlinSerializationJsonDecoder.java, KotlinSerializationJsonEncoder.java, ProtobufJsonEncoder.java, spring-mvc.xsd.

tasks.question: Since Spring Framework 7.0 the TestContext framework pauses inactive application contexts in the context cache and restarts them when they are needed again. When pausing or restarting Lifecycle components is slow, this slows down the whole test suite, so it must be possible to disable pausing completely through a JVM system property or Spring property named "spring.test.context.cache.pause", exposed as ContextCache.CONTEXT_CACHE_PAUSE_PROPERTY_NAME. Introduce a nested enum ContextCache.PauseMode with the constants ALWAYS (the default and the current behaviour) and NEVER (inactive contexts are never paused). Add a static method ContextCacheUtils.retrievePauseMode() that reads the property and returns ALWAYS when it is not set. It parses the value case-insensitively, ignoring leading and trailing whitespace. For an unknown value it throws an IllegalArgumentException with the message "Unsupported value '<value>' for property 'spring.test.context.cache.pause'". DefaultContextCache gets a new constructor DefaultContextCache(int maxSize, PauseMode pauseMode), and its existing constructors use the retrieved pause mode. With NEVER, a context is not paused when its last test class stops using it.
tasks.rationale: The commit adds the spring.test.context.cache.pause property with PauseMode ALWAYS/NEVER, the parsing logic in ContextCacheUtils, and a pause-mode-aware DefaultContextCache. The three spring-test types are primary because the tests call all of them directly. The remaining dependents are the SpringProperties Javadoc cross-reference in spring-core, the appendix and the context-caching AsciiDoc pages.

tasks.question: Resource responses ignore the If-Range request header: a Range request is always answered with 206 Partial Content, even when the If-Range validator no longer matches the current representation (RFC 9110, section 13.1.5). tasks.question: ResourceLoader#getResource does not support the "classpath*:" prefix: getResource("classpath*:META-INF/MANIFEST.MF") does not give access to all same-named resources on the classpath, which today requires ResourcePatternResolver#getResources. tasks.question: @Retryable method execution offers no way to observe the failures encountered during retries. Introduce an application event org.springframework.resilience.retry.MethodRetryEvent (an ApplicationEvent whose source is the MethodInvocation) with getMethod(), getFailure() returning the Throwable encountered, and isRetryAborted(). The retry interceptor publishes such an event through the application's event publisher whenever @Retryable processing is enabled in an application context: one event with isRetryAborted() == false for every failed attempt (exception thrown by the method or emitted by its returned reactive publisher), and one final event with isRetryAborted() == true when retrying gives up, whose failure is the RetryException for imperative methods or the terminal error of the retried publisher for reactive methods (for example the Reactor retry-exhausted exception, or a timeout exception). A successful attempt publishes no event. Separately, the RetryException thrown by RetryTemplate when interrupted during back-off should carry the message "Interrupted during back-off for retryable operation '<name>'; aborting execution".
